correctness.rationale: Exact diagonal covariance recursion gives all four schedule values; the dominated schedule is removed rigorously. Comparing the remaining three gives the displayed greedy and optimal costs and an if-and-only-if failure condition. A universal ratio bound follows by termwise comparison; a strictly positive-variance family tends to the same bound for each fixed diagonal dynamics. The separate zero-dynamics case and minimality are explicit. The Python standard-library verifier recomputes 20,000 rational cases and exact sharpness examples; infinite assertions rely on the algebraic proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The 2020 arbitrarily poor greedy phenomenon concerns static design-time steady-state selection and is not a counterexample to a bound for two-step dynamic sensing with fixed state gains. The general 2023 optimization formulation includes much broader instances algorithmically but does not assert or imply the exact sharp growth-dependent analytical bound. The 2016 indefinite-horizon work uses different sensing and objective conventions.

Qualitative greedy/submodularity findings do not establish the claimed exact worst-case constant for cumulative posterior trace.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The equivalent decision problem is choosing one of two perfect coordinate sensors at each of two instants, with cumulative posterior trace as loss, rather than subset selection or terminal covariance. The inspected finite-horizon formulation is more general in feasible schedules but reports computational solutions, not a closed form sharp multiplicative ratio in this restricted domain.

originality.rationale: This precise sharp two-time, cumulative-posterior-trace guarantee and exact failure criterion were not located in the examined main texts or compared research-record search results. Closest finite-horizon formulation solves combinatorial instances (Dutta et al., 2023); older greedy, hardness and remote-sensing papers have different objectives/horizons. Search nonidentification is not a novelty certificate; unexamined equivalent closed forms remain a stated priority risk.

value.rationale: Trace-greedy sensing is a natural computational baseline under a one-sensor-per-time constraint. The exact fixed-gain approximation constant quantifies how open-loop growth affects the value of one-step lookahead, is tight uniformly over the covariance/noise inputs, and distinguishes contractive versus arbitrarily expanding systems. The two-time two-state scope is minimal for strict greedy regret, making a meaningful boundary classification, not an arbitrary isolated numerical witness. Generalizations to noisy or dependent systems are not proved.
